business_scope.primary_industry_name: Dedicated Offshore Software Engineering and Maintenance Hub

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified under Taiwan Company Act, Civil Code, and related statutes; unitary national system with sub-national tax distinctions)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) signed on June 29, 2010 between Taiwan and Mainland China
Cross-Strait Bilateral Investment Protection Agreement (signed August 9, 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act (MLCA) and its Enforcement Rules, the Terrorism Financing Prevention Act, the Company Act Article 22-1 (as amended in 2018) requiring beneficial ownership declarations to the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) Law and Regulations Governing AML/CFT for Foreign Investment, and the Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland People for China-source investors. The Chinese parent company is additionally subject to PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (effective Nov 1, 2024). UBO data is stored in a government-only encrypted register; neither public inspection nor search-indexing is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Business License) of the Chinese parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC Notary Public -> Cross-Strait Notarization Verification via Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) in Taiwan (parallel to consular legalization; not Hague Apostille because neither China nor Taiwan is an Apostille member; do not chain apostille).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (existence certificate) of the Chinese parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR or designated enterprise credit authority in PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC Notary Public -> SEF Verification in Taiwan (Cross-Strait legalization procedure; mutually exclusive with Hague Apostille).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing formation of Taiwan JV and appointment of local representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of Chinese parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC Notary Public -> SEF Verification; certified English translation required, with traditional Chinese version notarized in Taiwan if necessary.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Taiwan JV Limited
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and local attorney (drafted in accordance with Taiwan Company Act)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before Taiwan court notary or certified public notary in Taiwan; no foreign authentication required for domestic instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (credit standing certificate) from the Chinese shareholder's bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank (e.g., ICBC, Bank of China) issuing in the name of the Chinese shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC Notary Public -> SEF Verification; bank's original seal must be authenticated; it is not subject to apostille or consular legalization in this cross-strait context.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), and senior managers must undergo mandatory screening against the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission's published lists, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and the cross-strait investment restriction database maintained by the MOEA Investment Commission. The screening must be refreshed every 30 days, not just at onboarding, and must cover direct, indirect, and beneficial ownership interests of 25% or more. Any PMLCA (Political Exposure) or adverse media hit will trigger enhanced due diligence, a risk rating escalation to High Risk, and a compliance hold until cleared by an independent AML officer. Documents must be face-to-face verified with passports and identity certificates; electronic verification is not acceptable for Chinese-source shareholders under the Qualified Mainland Investor rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MOEA Department of Commerce - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Examination System integrated into the Company Registration and Commerce Administration Service Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary company name must be in Traditional Chinese script, using the official national script. An English trade name may be registered as a secondary name but cannot be used as the sole statutory name. Four-tier review applies: (1) legal entity type suffix (Limited or Ltd.), (2) distinctive syllabic element, (3) business scope (software design, information services), (4) prohibition filter. Transliteration of the English shareholder name into Mandarin phonetics is accepted only if it does not produce a duplicate or an offending pun.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant (or a licensed local agent) may file an administrative appeal with the MOEA within 30 days of rejection. The appeal must include: (a) the rejected name and computerized pre-examination reference number, (b) a revised list of three alternative names, (c) written proof that the objectionable token is not part of the company's actual business (if the rejection was due to sensitive vocabulary), and (d) the MOEA rejection letter. The MOEA must respond within 15 working days. If the appeal is denied, a subsequent formal administrative remedy (appeal) before the Executive Yuan Appeals Commission is available within 30 days; thereafter, judicial review may be sought in the Taipei High Administrative Court. The name reservation cannot be extended beyond the initial 180-day window; a new application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Taiwan's Company Act requires a registered business office for service of process; however, a virtual office or commercial mailbox may be accepted for registration if it is a real licensed commercial address in Taiwan and the company can demonstrate that the address is not a PO Box. For an information-technology and software development offshore center (ISIC 6202), the Taipei National Tax Administration (NTRA) and the central bank (in foreign exchange matters) generally reject pure virtual offices when the entity has no physical staff or equipment. Banks, including Taiwan-based banks and foreign branch banks used for Wise B2B/Payoneer/Wire payments, will almost certainly require a physical on-site inspection before opening an account. Consequently, a virtual office is permissible only as an interim mailing address, but the company must secure a physical office lease (with zoning permitting office use) within 90 days of incorporation to satisfy commercial substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) presence of employees at the registered address during business hours; (2) office furniture, computing hardware, and servers or cloud-management terminals; (3) original lease agreement and utility bills in the company name; (4) business ledger and minutes. Quantified risk: moderate-low; approximately 15-20% annual probability of an unannounced inspection by the local National Tax Administration, 10% probability by the Company Registry, and 70% probability of a bank home-country inspection before account activation due to cross-strait investment enhanced due diligence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule under the Taiwan Company Act; for estimated capital of NTD 500,000, the fee is NTD 1,000 (approx. USD 33-40)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Chinese parent company documents (5 sets of copies) before a PRC notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provincial notary fee schedules; prevalent market benchmark is RMB 600-800 per notarial certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee schedule published by SEF; NTD 800 per application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm in Taipei (private legal fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and traditional Chinese certification of English documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate; NTD 2-4 per word with court notarization per page

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Articles 98 to 113 (limited company formation, shareholders, capital, directors, and registered office), Article 100 (full payment of subscribed capital), Article 387 (registration filing), and Articles 370 to 386 (foreign-invested companies); Foreign Investment Act, Articles 1 to 8; Regulations on Investment in Taiwan by Mainland China Investors, if the PRC shareholder is a mainland-incorporated entity; and Administrative Appeal Act for remedies against governmental decisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Development, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), R.O.C. (Taiwan); online company registration one-stop system at gcis.nat.gov.tw; for foreign and mainland China investors, Investment Commission, MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation of a Limited Company, together with supporting capital verification and investment approval certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Taiwan Companies Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-in capital; however, under Article 100, all subscribed capital contributions must be fully paid prior to filing the establishment registration. The funds must be remitted into the company's Taiwan bank account in New Taiwan Dollars or another legally convertible currency, and a bank-issued capital verification certificate confirming that the funds remain on deposit must be filed. No blocked escrow account is required under general rules; if the Investment Commission imposes conditions on mainland China-sourced investment, such conditions may include payment timing and use restrictions evidenced by bank statements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_JV_LTD (TAIWAN), A LIMITED COMPANY ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF CHINA (TAIWAN)

WHEREAS the shareholders of the Company have resolved to form a foreign-invested limited company and have subscribed to the registered capital set out in the Articles of Incorporation; and WHEREAS the Board is vested with the power to execute all acts necessary to complete statutory incorporation and commence operations; NOW, THEREFORE, the Board unanimously resolves as follows:

1. Capital Subscription and Issuance. The Board ratifies the subscription and allocation of the Company's registered share capital in the total amount of [INSERT AMOUNT], as set forth in the Articles. Each shareholder's capital contribution must be paid in full in cash to the Company's bank account in Taiwan before the establishment registration is filed. The statutory representative and the chief financial officer are authorized to execute all instruments and procure any capital verification certificates required to evidence full payment.

2. Banking and Payment Authorization. The Board authorizes the opening and operation of corporate bank and payment accounts at [INSERT BANK NAME], including electronic banking, Wise B2B, Payoneer, and SWIFT wire transfer facilities. Any two of the authorized signatories, namely the statutory representative, chief financial officer, and compliance officer, shall jointly approve disbursements above the internal threshold, and all account documents, mandates, and signature cards are ratified.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [INSERT ADDRESS], Taiwan, R.O.C. The statutory representative is directed to file the registered office with the Department of Commercial Development, Ministry of Economic Affairs, to keep the corporate seal and statutory records there, and to notify the registry promptly of any change.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [NAME] as Director and statutory representative, [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. Each officer accepts all legal duties under the Companies Act and is vested with authority to sign tax returns, employment registrations, bank forms, and all government filings.

5. Ratification of Governance Documents. The Articles of Incorporation, shareholders' agreement, and bank capital verification are ratified and approved. The officers are directed to submit the company establishment registration application and to take all steps necessary to obtain the Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number.

6. Effectiveness. This resolution is effective immediately upon unanimous adoption, and a certified copy shall be inserted in the corporate minute book and provided to banks, tax authorities, and counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign and Mainland China Investment Approval plus Company Name and Business Scope Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC); Company Name and Business Scope Online Reservation Portal, Department of Commercial Development, MOEA, gcis.nat.gov.tw
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company name and business-scope pre-review application through the MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Reservation Portal. Simultaneously, if any shareholder is a foreign entity or a mainland China-invested entity, file a foreign investment application with the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs. In the application, disclose ultimate beneficial owners, source of funds, and the proposed offshore development center business plan. Notarize the joint venture agreement and Articles in the investor's home country; legalize and translate them into Chinese for the Investment Commission's administrative record. The Investment Commission approval letter must be attached when filing company registration.
required_dossiers: MOEA company name and business scope pre-review application form
Foreign investment application form (if applicable)
Notarized and legalized joint venture or shareholders agreement
Notarized and legalized draft Articles of Incorporation
Business plan for the offshore development center
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution of each corporate shareholder
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds evidence
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan statutory representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried or suspended, the applicant has a statutory window to submit supplementary documentation through the Investment Commission portal. If approval is denied, the shareholder may file a written appeal to the Investment Commission under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days, restructure the shareholding or business scope, or resubmit a fresh application without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization, and Paid-in Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan district court notary office or licensed notary; licensed bank in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and notarize the Articles of Incorporation, the shareholders' agreement, and the first board resolution. Each shareholder must sign before a Taiwan notary, with foreign documents legalized and accompanied by certified Chinese translation. Open the company's bank account, remit the full subscribed capital, and obtain a capital verification certificate from the bank stating the amount paid in and that funds remain on deposit. Also notarize the director's written consent and each officer's acceptance. This step satisfies the full paid-up capital rule under Article 100 of the Companies Act before the establishment application is submitted.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Incorporation signed by all shareholders
Shareholders' agreement executed by all parties
First Board of Directors Resolution
Bank capital verification certificate
Notarized director consent and officer acceptance forms
Legalized and translated foreign documents
Passport or national ID copies of all shareholders and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or bank rejects any document, correct translation or legalization deficiencies and re-notarize; request a corrected capital verification certificate. A bank failure to issue the certificate can be cured by obtaining an electronic bank statement and a letter from another licensed bank, or by selecting a new bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Development, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Central Company Registration One-Stop Portal, gcis.nat.gov.tw
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Central Company Registration Portal of the Department of Commercial Development, MOEA. Select limited company establishment, complete all company particulars, and upload the approved name reservation, notarized Articles, capital verification certificate, Investment Commission approval, registered-office lease or owner consent, and officer appointment consents. Pay the NT$1,000 statutory filing fee and sign the application electronically by the statutory representative using the portal's authentication mechanism. The registrar will examine compliance under the Companies Act, issue the Company Registration Certificate, and assign the Unified Business Number.
required_dossiers: Approved company name reservation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital verification certificate from the bank
Investment Commission foreign or mainland China investment approval
Registered office lease or owner's written consent
Director and officer appointment consents
Company establishment registration application form generated by the portal
Filing fee remittance record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar challenges any defect, cure by filing an amendment or supplement request through the same portal within the deadline stated in the deficiency notice. If refused, file an appeal or administrative remedy within 30 days, or resubmit after correction; expedited cure is possible by pre-clearing documents with registry staff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Labor, Health Insurance, and Foreign Trade Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Labor Insurance Administration; National Health Insurance Administration; Bureau of Foreign Trade, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number to register the profit-seeking enterprise at the local National Taxation Bureau, apply for uniform invoice registration, and obtain the tax identification number. Register as an employer with the Labor Insurance Administration and the National Health Insurance Administration. If the company will remit service fees abroad, register export or import service records with the Bureau of Foreign Trade. Submit the Articles, lease, capital verification certificate, employment contracts, and payroll list. Keep all records for at least five years for tax audit.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number
Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution
Registered office lease or ownership certificate
Capital verification certificate
Employment contracts and payroll list for initial staff
Tax registration and uniform invoice application forms
Foreign trade service registration form for Bureau of Foreign Trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau or labor authority issues a correction, reply with the correct forms and pay any prescribed late fee before assessment. If a penalty is assessed, file a formal protest with the tax authority within 30 days and thereafter pursue review by the administrative appeal committee of the Ministry of Finance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Cross-Border Payment Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank in Taiwan; Wise B2B and Payoneer payment service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Company Registration Certificate, notarized Articles, first board resolution, and identification documents of beneficial owners and authorized signatories to the selected Taiwanese bank. Complete KYC and AML forms and beneficial ownership declarations, execute specimen signature cards and online banking mandates, and activate Wise B2B, Payoneer, and SWIFT wire payment agreements. The bank verifies corporate existence against the MOEA company registry, may require source-of-funds evidence, and will issue corporate banking tokens and payment credentials after compliance screening is completed.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
First Board Resolution authorizing bank accounts
Passport of statutory representative and authorized signatories
Beneficial ownership declaration and AML/KYC forms
Bank account application and specimen signature card
Agreements with Wise B2B and Payoneer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC or AML information, provide the specified source-of-funds and ultimate beneficial ownership evidence within the bank's deadline. If account opening is denied, apply to another licensed bank and update the corporate records with new signing authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (R.O.C.) - National Taxation Bureau with local jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing is conducted through the Ministry of Finance Tax Entry Portal and the E-Invoice Integration Service Platform. The People's Republic of China State Taxation Administration is not the registration authority for the Taiwan-registered entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Obtain foreign investment approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) if the non-resident shareholder holds equity in the Taiwan entity. Step 2 - File company name reservation and company registration with MOEA; for a foreign investor, register as a Taiwan limited company or as a branch of a foreign company and appoint a local statutory agent. Step 3 - Within 15 days after completed company registration, file an application for tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau having jurisdiction over the principal office. Step 4 - The National Taxation Bureau will assign a Unified Business Number (UBIN), which serves as the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and Business Tax registration number. Step 5 - Register as a Uniform Invoice user and, if electronic invoices are adopted, obtain an MOF-issued certificate and enrol in the E-Invoice Turnkey Platform. Step 6 - Register as a withholding tax agent for payroll and for payments of dividends, royalties, service fees, or interest to non-residents. Step 7 - Register with the Customs Administration only when physical goods or software media are imported or exported; pure electronic software services require no customs registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture or for a Taiwan-registered limited company/branch. The Taiwan entity is taxed as a resident limited-liability profit-seeking enterprise; shareholders are not permitted to pass through the Taiwan entity's taxable income. Certain tax consolidation treatments exist only following a statutory merger or approved group restructuring under the Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Act, but no general entity-classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (VAT) under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For incorporated JV entities there is no turnover threshold; all incorporated businesses must complete tax registration and file Business Tax. For non-incorporated sole proprietorships, tax registration is mandatory when average monthly sales exceed NT$80,000 for goods or NT$40,000 for services. A simplified small-business scheme with a lower tax rate and no Uniform Invoice requirement is available below NT$200,000 average monthly sales; once NT$200,000 is exceeded, full Uniform Invoice-issuing VAT registration is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan requires all VAT businesses to issue Uniform Invoices for taxable domestic supplies. Electronic Uniform Invoices (E-Invoices) are transmitted through the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Service Platform using the E-Invoice Turnkey API; XML invoice data must be uploaded within 48 hours of issuance. This is not a point-of-sale real-time fiscal clearance mandate for ordinary B2B software services. B2C E-Invoices must contain a QR code, carrier number, and an invoice number allocated from the MOF Uniform Invoice numbering sequence to support anti-fraud checks and the Uniform Invoice lottery. The Turnkey API requires MOF-issued digital certificates, TLS transport, and XML schema validation; equivalent anti-fraud integrity is achieved through certificate-authenticated payload transmission rather than a per-invoice fiscal stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating is available under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act. The Taiwan JV may zero-rate software engineering and maintenance services when: (1) the services are sold to a foreign buyer; (2) the services are rendered in Taiwan but used by the foreign buyer outside Taiwan, or the services are directly related to the export of goods; (3) the consideration is paid in foreign exchange; and (4) the foreign exchange proceeds are actually repatriated to and received in Taiwan. The zero-rating is claimed on the seller's Business Tax return; failure to document any element converts the supply to a taxable supply at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry / Bill of Entry) issued by Taiwan Customs for physical goods, mandatory when software is exported on physical media
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment outside Taiwan, if applicable
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Receipt from an authorized bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency
Commercial invoice or revenue invoice issued under the Uniform Invoice system and explicitly marked zero-rated
Sales contract or purchase order with the foreign buyer identifying the service scope and offshore user
Service delivery and usage evidence such as an electronic acceptance report, SLA log, time sheet, or server off-site proof showing that the software engineering service was consumed outside Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau cross-matches zero-rated sales against export declarations, Uniform Invoice records, and FIRC or foreign exchange settlement receipts. If supporting documents are missing, incomplete, or inconsistent, the zero-rating is disallowed and the tax authority will retroactively assess 5% Business Tax on the gross consideration plus overdue interest and an administrative penalty generally up to five times the underpaid tax under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act. If forged or false documents are used, criminal liability for tax evasion and document forgery can be charged under the Tax Collection Act and the Criminal Code, and the responsible person may be subject to imprisonment. A 180-day foreign exchange realization period is applied to export proceeds; unrepatriated amounts may be reclassified as taxable domestic sales unless the taxpayer obtains an approved maturity extension from the Central Bank.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), acting with the Financial Supervisory Commission for banking conduct; foreign exchange operations are delegated to authorized foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan Dollar is convertible for current account trade and service transactions, including cross-border software development fees under an ODC model, through authorized foreign exchange banks. There is no centralized surrender of all receipts, but every inward and outward settlement must be reported through the CBC-compliant banking system. Capital account convertibility is conditional: inbound equity investment from a mainland China parent into the Taiwan joint venture requires prior approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. Once the approved capital is received, the foreign currency can be converted to TWD only after the bank checks the approval letter, company resolution, and source-of-funds evidence. Profit and dividend remittances are allowed after corporate income tax and withholding tax obligations are fully paid, provided the audited financial statements, tax certificates, and board dividend resolution are submitted to the bank. The CBC may impose additional declarations or retention restrictions during external imbalances, and mainland-origin investors face stricter national security review and cross-strait investment screening; therefore a simple automatic convertibility route is not available. The regime is a declaration-based supervisory model, not a full surrender regime, but non-compliance triggers severe penalties and account freezing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from ODC services must be collected through an authorized bank within 180 days from the service completion or invoice date; once credited, 100% of the export proceeds are converted into New Taiwan Dollars by default within two business days. A foreign currency retention quota may be approved for documented operational needs such as cloud hosting, offshore salaries, and license fees, but the retained amount remains subject to monthly CBC reporting. Extension of the 180-day collection period requires a written CBC approval before the original expiry.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for inbound investment and capital verification
Basic Operational Currency Account (TWD plus USD multi-currency)
Basic Operational Currency Account with Offshore Banking Unit support
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a standalone treasury account. Wise and Payoneer are not licensed authorized foreign exchange banks or electronic payment institutions with NT-dollar deposit-taking authority, and they cannot execute CBC foreign exchange declarations, capital verification, or escrow compliance. They may only be used as supplemental collection rails for low-value overseas invoices after the Taiwan bank account is active. Any attempt to route mainland China capital injection or ODC payroll through an EMI would trigger automatic AML review and probable rejection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence at a Taiwan branch is mandatory for at least one statutory director and the designated finance officer for original identity and signature KYC. Remote foreign directors may use a consular-certified power of attorney authenticated by a Taiwan overseas mission, but the first account opening interview must be performed in-branch by the authorized representative; videoconference KYC is only a supplement. The bank will also request a live board meeting excerpt confirming the authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain with mainland China individual shareholders and nominee-like layered entities around the Taiwan JV.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified group ownership chart covering all entities; notarized shareholder registry; passports or national IDs of every ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-wealth questionnaires; three years of audited financial statements; tax returns; and a board-certified negative confirmation that no nominee shareholding exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ODC revenue model consisting mainly of service fees to a related foreign parent, raising fabricated-invoice and transfer-mispricing risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master software development agreement; project work orders and milestone acceptance reports; code repository access logs; engineer payroll and social insurance records; ERP invoice and settlement history; OECD transfer pricing benchmarking study; contemporaneous TP documentation; and an operational substance report with headcount and office lease.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from mainland China into a Taiwan entity, exposing the bank to cross-strait investment and national security non-compliance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MOEA Investment Commission approval letter; CBC foreign exchange declaration forms; board capital injection resolution; source funding bank statements from the mainland parent; projected ODC cash flow model; and an undertaking that funds will be used only for approved software engineering and maintenance operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Possible dual-use technology or export-control exposure if ODC clients include sensitive semiconductor, telecom, or military-adjacent end users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed technology scope with ISIC/NAICS classification; end-user and end-use certificates; export-control classification matrix; sanctions screening report from a recognized compliance database; internal security policy; IP access controls; and an audit trail of client onboarding reviews.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the CN parent to fund the Taiwan JV: (1) secure Investment Commission approval for the mainland investor before sending funds; (2) open a TWD capital escrow account and a multi-currency operational account at Bank of Taiwan or another designated tier-1 bank; (3) remit via SWIFT MT103 with the CBC foreign exchange declaration purpose code for direct investment/equity injection; the remittance narrative must include the approval number and JV registration reference; (4) do not convert to TWD until the bank confirms the Investment Commission approval and source-of-funds documentation; (5) after clearing, obtain a Taiwan CPA capital verification report based on the original bank confirmation letter; (6) transfer escrowed capital into the operational account only after all corporate and tax registrations are complete. Any deviation in purpose code or beneficiary naming will trigger quarantine and AML escalation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for vendor payments, payroll, cloud infrastructure, and license fees; commercial documentary collections for deferred service invoices; and commercial or standby letters of credit for hardware procurement and milestone-bound software contracts where bank payment undertakings are required. All outgoing settlements must be matched to an underlying ODC contract, carry the invoice and work-order reference, and be declared under the applicable CBC current-account transaction code. For payments to mainland China counterparties, use USD or TWD clearing through the bank's offshore banking unit or an approved trade settlement rail with full BOA reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright USD/TWD forward contracts based on actual software-export invoices and committed receivables
Plain-vanilla FX options with an approved CBC/bank credit facility and genuine underlying trade exposure
Cross-currency swaps for long-term capital exposure backed by the approved investment structure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not generally permissible onshore for Taiwan entities; such instruments may be considered in the offshore banking unit only for non-resident counterparties and only with strict underlying trade justification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual financial statements and profit-distribution resolution (Company Act Article 230 filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting to be held by 30 June; filing within 15 days after AGM approval (i.e., by 15 July for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$10,000–NT$100,000 per occurrence; continued non-compliance may trigger compulsory rectification orders and dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and accompanying financial report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local branch)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May following the fiscal year-end (calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of up to 15% of the tax due, daily interest, administrative fines, and criminal liability for willful tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested company operation report (under the Foreign Investment Law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000; serious or repeated failure may result in revocation of foreign investment approval.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit by a certified public accountant is required for companies with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million (approx. USD 1 million). The competent authority may also impose audit requirements based on scale, public interest, or foreign investment conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public companies must apply the Taiwan Business Entity Accounting Act and Taiwan/ROC GAAP (substantially IFRS-converged); publicly listed companies must apply Taiwan IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO re-declaration is required under Taiwan law. UBO information must be updated in the company’s UBO register and registered with MOEA within 15 days of any shareholding transfer or ownership change. The corporate secretary should obtain signed shareholder/director confirmations at the annual general meeting to verify the accuracy of the UBO and share registers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250 – US$750 (annual registered office service and local corporate agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000 – US$10,000 (typical certified audit fee for a small-to-mid-size JV)

stage_6.infraction_category: Area of violation (e.g. Tax Evasion, Shell Company, AML)
stage_6.statutory_sanction: Specific legal sanction and financial penalty
stage_6.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment
